tagline: From sagebrush plateaus to mountain overlooks, a road circles the Wallowas.
intro: The Hells Canyon Scenic Byway circles the Wallowa Mountains between Baker City and La Grande, passing sagebrush plateaus, farms and mountain overlooks. Parts of the road are narrow and winding; Oregon’s transportation department gives the 218-mile journey a minimum of eight to ten hours. The Federal Highway Administration describes this All-American Road through its contrasts: riverbanks, mountain heights, basalt cliffs and cultivated valley floors.

Travel along parts of the Baker-Copperfield route predates the scenic designation: emigrants used portions on their way to the Willamette Valley in the early 1840s. Gold discoveries brought another wave of settlers in the 1860s, followed by people drawn to timber and farmland. The modern corridor became a National Forest Scenic Byway in 1992, an Oregon State Scenic Byway in 1997 and an All-American Road in 2000.

From Baker City, follow Oregon Route 86 east through Richland and Halfway, then Forest Road 39 toward the Hells Canyon Overlook spur. The forest road crosses the Imnaha River and turns west toward Joseph, with Wallowa Lake a mile south of town. Route 82 continues through Enterprise and Wallowa, enters the Wallowa River canyon and climbs the steep Minam Grade. Beyond Elgin, the drive ends in the Grande Ronde Valley at La Grande.

moments.title: Halfway
moments.text: Halfway’s dot-com-era name change was a publicity proclamation, not a legal renaming. Its latitude was part of the pitch: the town lies close to the midpoint between the equator and the North Pole. In December 1999, the town accepted an offer to call itself Half.com for one year in exchange for $110,000, twenty school computers and other subsidies. Two signs went up at its borders announcing the promotion. One acquired a second life at auction in 2007, when Half.com founder Josh Kopelman bought it for $1,000. ODOT describes Halfway as a departure point for Hells Canyon adventures.

moments.title: Hells Canyon Overlook
moments.text: The paved Hells Canyon Overlook stands at 5,400 feet, reached by a spur from Forest Road 39 via Forest Road 3965. Its view takes in McGraw Creek, Hells Canyon and the Seven Devils Mountains at the Idaho border. Interpretive displays explain the canyon’s formation. Continuing north on Forest Road 39 brings the route across the Imnaha River before it turns west toward the Wallowa Mountains.
moments.notice: The overlook faces McGraw Creek, Hells Canyon and the Seven Devils Mountains.

moments.title: Wallowa Lake
moments.text: A mile south of Joseph, Wallowa Lake is held between high moraines left by Pleistocene glaciers. These ridges begin below the water and rise more than 900 feet above it. The lake has appeared in geology textbooks as an example of water dammed by moraines. A later dam at the northern outlet was built for irrigation in 1918 and raised in 1929. That concrete structure stands thirty-five feet high and supplies irrigation without generating hydroelectric power; local irrigation consumers own and operate it. Wallowa Lake State Park occupies the southern shore.

practical: Hells Canyon Overlook: ODOT lists Forest Road 39 as snow-closed October 15 through May 15. Between Joseph and Halfway, stretches exceed eighty miles without gas. (checked 2026-10-11)
